full_inspection: All four complete native images of copy1site052 and copy2site128 were inspected. Every body line, paragraph, punctuation, space and margin was compared. audit_128_details.jpg records the overstrike and the extra points in the word gaps. The shared double space after goût and the copy-specific foliation were also directly checked. Apart from the seven recorded loci, the body readings agree.
original_transcription_comparison: Both original transcriptions were compared in full. The copy2 overstrike was confirmed, resolving its u and qualifying its covered e. The source omitted the observed double space and four small traces, now recorded with uncertainty. The archive and scan metadata are copy-specific.

entries.decision: retain the copy2-only low point with unresolved status
entries.reason: The short low point after à is visible in copy2 and absent from copy1. This records the body-reading difference without assigning origin or textual role.

entries.decision: retain the clear u overwrite and doubtful lower e
entries.reason: The clear manuscript u covers the typed e position. The lower e is substantially obscured in copy2 and keeps explicit doubt, although copy1 clearly has e.

entries.decision: restore the observed double space in copy2
entries.reason: Both native upper halves show the same doubled gap between goût and et. The supplied copy2 source had collapsed it to one space.

entries.decision: retain the copy2 point-shaped margin trace without assigning a hand
entries.reason: A dark point is visible in the left margin beside qu’acceptable. Its origin and role remain unresolved; the doubtful margin marker preserves its shape and location.

The small point after pour sits higher in the gap, around mid-letter height, and is absent in copy1. The centered text glyph records the observed location without inferring a mathematical sign or origin.
The low point before moindre is visible in copy2 and absent in copy1. Its origin and textual role remain unresolved.
The lower-left inscriptions clearly read52 and128. No authorship attribution is made.
